text.p: Italian debt futures ended higher but with underlying sentiment weak as the market watched the lira's performance against the mark and for signals on a possible EMU delay and the domestic Italian scene.
The March Liffe Btp contract, which rolls over into June on Tuesday, ended 50 basis points up at 128.00 but off a day's high of 128.14.
Traders said March jumped 100 bps from an early low of 126.95 on news Italian PSBR in the first two months of 1997 was around 6.5 trillion lire, down from 25.7 trillion in the same 1995 period.
This morning dealers saw the Bank of Italy selling marks at around the lira low of 1,003.60 per mark.

U.S. Treasuries were steady after the February NAPM index came in as expected, at 53.1 against 52.0 in January. Attention now turns to the second part of Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony Wednesday and U.S. jobs data Friday.
Traders said the Italian market was vulnerable due to worries over a possible delay to EMU and uncertainties over the process of restoring Italian accounts to health for membership.
"The destiny of Btps doesn't just depend on decisions taken in Rome but on signals from Bonn and Frankfurt," one said.

"The uncertainty about Germany's ability to meet the Maastricht goals will remain, but we will have some clues about this on Thursday with February jobless data," said Ilaria Fornari, economist at JP Morgan in Milano.
Today German Finance Minister Theo Waigel denied rumours February unemployment hit a record 4.8 million, saying he expected it to show a slight rise from January's 4.66 million.

Giuseppe Abbotto of Indosuez saw the spread over the benchmark 10-year bund staying around 200 bps with the risk of it widening out further depending on the government of Romano Prodi's decision over a corrective mini-budget.
